name: Internet content

subjectOf.text: Newspapers, record labels, broadcast networks, and publishing houses did not merely lose market share under zero marginal cost distribution; their foundational business models became structurally incoherent because those models assumed distribution was scarce and costly.
subjectOf.abstract: Their foundational business models, built on the assumption that distribution was scarce and costly, became structurally incoherent.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, The Collapse of Scarcity Economics (2026). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=6421319
scope_conditions: observed in the internet content economy

subjectOf.text: The internet content case shows that when one form of scarcity disappears, economic power migrates to whoever controls the next binding constraint, which for internet content was the platform infrastructure for discovery and distribution rather than the content itself.
subjectOf.abstract: This last observation directly reinforces the binding-constraint analysis in Section II.D: when one form of scarcity disappears, economic power migrates to whoever controls the next binding constraint.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, The Collapse of Scarcity Economics (2026). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=6421319
scope_conditions: generalized from platform intermediaries such as Google, Meta, and Amazon
